Frequently Asked Questions

These are the questions researchers ask most often about this category of compounds. Because it holds both peptides and small molecules, several answers differ by compound.

What are Metabolic & GLP-1 Compounds?

Metabolic & GLP-1 Compounds is our category for compounds used in laboratory research on glucose handling, appetite signalling and cell energy metabolism. It holds incretin peptides, such as semaglutide and tirzepatide, which act on the GLP-1 receptor, alongside small molecules such as 5-amino-1MQ and AICAR, which act on enzymes inside cells. Nothing in this category is a weight-loss product. Human data for the incretin peptides comes from trials of licensed medicines, and for the small molecules there is essentially none. Supplied for laboratory research use only, not for human or veterinary use.

How Do Metabolic & GLP-1 Compounds Work?

In research models, semaglutide binds the GLP-1 receptor, found on insulin-producing cells in the pancreas and on nerve cells in the gut and brain. Tirzepatide binds the GLP-1 receptor and the GIP receptor, a second incretin receptor. Both carry a fatty-acid chain that binds albumin, which keeps them in circulation for days. 5-amino-1MQ blocks NNMT, an enzyme active in fat cells, and AICAR activates AMPK, the enzyme cells use to sense low energy. These descriptions come from laboratory and pharmacology research and establish no use outside the laboratory.

How are Metabolic & GLP-1 Compounds Typically Stored and Handled?

Most products in this category ship as lyophilized, or freeze-dried, powder in sealed vials. Store them refrigerated from arrival, away from light, heat and moisture, and keep each vial sealed until reconstitution; freezing the dry powder is an option for longer storage. Bacteriostatic water is the usual fluid, and our vials hold 3 ml, so reconstitution volumes stay within that. Add the water slowly down the inside wall of the vial and swirl gently rather than shaking. Use sterile technique throughout. The lipotropic blend is supplied differently, so check its product page for storage conditions.

What are the Common Research Applications of Metabolic & GLP-1 Compounds?

Published laboratory work on this class falls into a few areas. Receptor studies measure how each peptide binds and activates the GLP-1 and GIP receptors. Pancreatic cell studies track insulin release. Rodent studies follow glucose handling and food intake under controlled diets. Cell studies of 5-amino-1MQ and AICAR measure enzyme activity and energy use in fat, muscle and liver cells. Much of the human literature on semaglutide and tirzepatide comes from trials of licensed medicines, which does not transfer to research material.

When Can I Expect My Metabolic & GLP-1 Compounds Delivery?

Orders are typically delivered within 2–4 business days from the date the order is placed. Delivery is within Costa Rica only. Timing can vary with carrier schedules, the delivery province and order processing. We confirm stock and the expected delivery window with you before an order is finalized.

Nootropic & Neuropeptides

Nootropic and neuropeptide research looks at short peptides studied for their activity in the nervous system. This category holds three synthetic peptides: Selank and Semax, both developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences, and Adamax, a newer analogue built on the Semax structure. Peptides Costa Rica supplies them as research-grade material, with independent batch testing and delivery within Costa Rica. Everything here is supplied for laboratory research use only.

Nootropic & Neuropeptides Origin

Selank and Semax are both short synthetic peptides built on natural templates. Selank is based on tuftsin, a four-amino-acid peptide found in the body, extended with three more amino acids for stability. Semax is based on a short fragment of ACTH, the adrenocorticotropic hormone, extended in the same way.

Most published work on both comes from Russian research groups and uses rodent models. Adamax, a newer Semax analogue, has almost no dedicated published research of its own; what is written about it is largely borrowed from Semax.

Peptides Costa Rica supplies these compounds as research-grade material, with clear product information, honest pricing and dependable local service in Costa Rica.

 

Nootropic & Neuropeptides

Buy Nootropic & Neuropeptides: Research Grade & Lab Tested

Nootropic and neuropeptides are supplied here as research-grade material. The category holds Selank 10mg, Semax 10mg and Adamax in 5mg and 10mg vials, each a lyophilized powder in a sealed vial that is reconstituted with bacteriostatic water before laboratory use. Sleep-related peptides such as DSIP sit in their own category. Every batch is tested by an independent laboratory for identity and purity, and the certificate of analysis is available for the lot you receive. For Adamax in particular, the certificate is worth reading closely, because the name is used for more than one version of the molecule across the market.

Prices are listed per vial on each product page and updated as stock moves. Delivery is within Costa Rica only and usually takes two to four business days, with free shipping on orders above $200 and bulk pricing on five or more vials of the same product. Our team can confirm availability, vial size and the expected delivery window before you order, and can send the certificate of analysis for a specific lot on request.

The Compounds in This Category

Selank

A seven-amino-acid peptide, Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro, developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences as a stabilized analogue of tuftsin. Published work is mostly in rats and mice, where studies have measured changes in brain neurotransmitter levels and in gene expression, including BDNF in the hippocampus. Research on it has largely come from the group that developed it.

Semax

A seven-amino-acid peptide, Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro, based on a short fragment of ACTH, the adrenocorticotropic hormone. Animal studies have measured changes in BDNF and its receptor in the hippocampus, and in brain serotonin and dopamine systems. It has the largest published literature of the three compounds in this category, most of it from Russian research groups. It is also the reference compound against which newer analogues in this family are usually described.

Adamax

A newer synthetic analogue built on the Semax backbone. Suppliers sell versions with and without an added adamantane group, which changes the molecular weight, so the certificate of analysis for the lot matters more than usual. There is essentially no dedicated peer-reviewed research on Adamax itself, and statements about it are generally extrapolated from Semax.

Reading the Research

Almost all of the work in this category is preclinical, and much of it comes from a small number of research groups. A change measured in rodent brain tissue is a laboratory finding, not evidence of an effect in a person. For Adamax, there is very little published research to read at all, which is worth knowing before designing a study around it.

Bioregulator Peptides

Bioregulator peptides are very short peptides, usually two to four amino acids long, that grew out of research begun in the 1970s at the Military Medical Academy in Leningrad and continued at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology. This category covers Epithalon, Pinealon, Cartalax and Thymalin. Peptides Costa Rica supplies them as research-grade material, with independent batch testing and delivery within Costa Rica. Everything here is supplied for laboratory research use only.

Where Bioregulator Peptides Come From

The first bioregulators were not synthetic. They were polypeptide extracts taken from animal organs, such as thymalin from thymus tissue and epithalamin from the pineal gland. From the 1990s, researchers identified short sequences thought to carry the activity of those extracts and began making them synthetically.

The central idea is that very short peptides can act as tissue-specific signals at the level of gene expression. That remains a hypothesis rather than an established mechanism, and most of the published work comes from one research group and its collaborators.

Peptides Costa Rica supplies these compounds as research-grade material, with clear product information, honest pricing and dependable local delivery in Costa Rica.

The Compounds in This Category

Epithalon

A four-amino-acid peptide, Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly, developed as a synthetic counterpart to epithalamin, a pineal gland extract. It is by some distance the most studied compound in the class. Published work includes telomerase activity in cultured human cells and pineal and melatonin measures in animal models, nearly all of it from the same research network.

Pinealon

A three-amino-acid peptide, Glu-Asp-Arg. It appears in research on brain tissue, including cell-culture and animal models examining neuronal cells under stress conditions. The body of published work on it is small, and the compound is far less studied than Epithalon.

Cartalax

A three-amino-acid peptide, Ala-Glu-Asp, associated in the literature with cartilage tissue. Published studies examine it in chondrocyte and fibroblast cultures, looking at gene expression and cell behavior. As with most of this class, independent replication outside the originating research group is limited.

Thymalin

Originally a polypeptide fraction isolated from thymus tissue rather than a single defined sequence, which makes it the oldest compound in the class. It appears in immunology research, mostly older animal work and small observational studies. Its later synthetic descendant, Thymogen (Glu-Trp), is a separate compound.

Collagen peptides are short amino-acid chains produced by breaking down collagen, a structural protein. In laboratory research, these fragments are examined for their composition, peptide sequences, and behavior in experimental systems. The term describes a family of materials rather than one compound with a fixed formula. This page explains that category and distinguishes collagen-derived materials from GHK-Cu, the copper peptide currently shown below. Peptides Costa Rica supplies research materials with local stock confirmation and delivery within Costa Rica only.

What Are Collagen Peptides?

Collagen consists of long protein chains arranged in a triple helix. Hydrolysis breaks those chains into smaller fragments called collagen peptides. A collagen hydrolysate usually contains a mixture of fragments with different sequences and molecular weights.

Researchers may work with that mixture or examine an individual collagen-derived sequence. Examples include prolyl-hydroxyproline, abbreviated Pro-Hyp, and hydroxyprolyl-glycine, abbreviated Hyp-Gly. A named sequence and a mixed hydrolysate are different types of research material.

The source collagen and processing method influence the resulting composition. Describing a material simply as “collagen peptides” therefore leaves important questions about its identity, peptide profile, and experimental relevance unanswered.

How Are Collagen Peptides Used in Laboratory Research?

Laboratory research on collagen peptides includes chemical characterization and experiments with defined peptide sequences. Researchers ask which fragments are present, how samples differ, and whether experimental conditions change the observations. These are questions about materials and laboratory models. They do not establish a personal application for a research vial or make different peptides interchangeable.

Peptide Identification and Profiling

Chromatography separates components of a collagen hydrolysate, while mass spectrometry helps characterize peptide masses and sequences. Researchers use these methods to describe a sample's peptide profile. A total protein figure alone cannot show which individual fragments are present or how they are distributed throughout the mixture.

Experiments in Cell-Culture Models

Collagen-derived peptides are also examined in cell-culture experiments, including studies using fibroblasts. Researchers measure endpoints such as cell numbers under defined experimental conditions. Background components in culture media can influence those measurements, so appropriate controls matter. These experiments describe observations in a laboratory model; they do not demonstrate what a supplier's vial will do in a person or establish a personal-use recommendation.

Comparing Individual Peptide Sequences

Some experiments focus on individual collagen-derived peptides, such as Pro-Hyp or Hyp-Gly, rather than an entire hydrolysate. Defined materials allow researchers to compare specific sequences and distinguish their observations from those obtained with a complex mixture. The exact peptide identity matters: sharing a collagen-related research topic does not make two compounds equivalent or establish that one can replace another experimentally.

Batch and Analytical Method Comparisons

Collagen hydrolysates can differ between batches, even when sold under the same general description. Analytical research compares peptide distributions and examines whether different measurement methods describe those samples consistently. This work helps define material specifications and identify variation that could affect experimental comparisons. Results remain tied to the tested samples, methods, and conditions; they are not a blanket certification of all collagen products.

What are collagen peptides?

Collagen peptides are short amino acid chains produced by breaking collagen down through hydrolysis. Reproductive signaling research looks at the peptides and hormones that carry signals through the reproductive endocrine system, from the brain to the pituitary gland and on to other tissues. Reproductive Signalling Peptides

The compounds in this category are studied for their roles in hormonal signaling within the reproductive endocrine system. Research looks at how each one acts on a specific receptor, and how those signals pass between the brain, the pituitary gland and other tissues.

They are not all the same kind of molecule. Oxytocin, PT-141 and kisspeptin-10 are short peptides of nine, seven and ten amino acids. hCG is a much larger glycoprotein hormone, which is why it is supplied in international units rather than milligrams.

The Compounds in This Category

Oxytocin

A nine-amino-acid peptide hormone, Cys-Tyr-Ile-Gln-Asn-Cys-Pro-Leu-Gly-NH2, with a bridge between its two cysteines that closes part of it into a ring. It is made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary. In 1953 it became the first peptide hormone to be synthesized in a laboratory. Research uses it to study receptor signaling in tissue and animal models.

PT-141

Also known as bremelanotide, a seven-amino-acid cyclic peptide related to melanotan II and to the natural hormone alpha-MSH. It acts on melanocortin receptors, mainly MC3R and MC4R, which are expressed in the brain. Research uses it to study central melanocortin signaling, largely in animal models.

Kisspeptin-10

The ten-amino-acid C-terminal fragment of kisspeptin, a peptide encoded by the KISS1 gene. It binds the KISS1 receptor, also called GPR54, on neurons that release gonadotropin-releasing hormone. Research uses it to study how signals travel along the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis.

hCG

Human chorionic gonadotropin is a glycoprotein hormone of 237 amino acids across two subunits, far larger than the other three compounds here. It binds the same receptor as luteinizing hormone. Because its activity is standardized biologically rather than by weight, it is supplied in international units.

What Are Mitochondrial Compounds

Mitochondria turn nutrients into ATP, the molecule cells use to carry energy, and they sit at the center of a large body of cell and animal research. The compounds in this category are studied for how they interact with mitochondria or with the pathways that regulate them.

They get there in very different ways. SS-31 is designed to reach the inner mitochondrial membrane directly. MOTS-c is itself encoded in mitochondrial DNA. NAD+ is a coenzyme that mitochondria depend on. SLU-PP-332 acts on receptors involved in regulating mitochondrial and metabolic genes.

Growth hormone secretagogues are a separate class with their own category. Compounds are supplied in sealed vials, most as a lyophilized powder that is reconstituted with bacteriostatic water before laboratory use, and the product page states the form for each listing. Common Compounds in This Category

SS-31

A four-amino-acid peptide, D-Arg-Dmt-Lys-Phe-NH2, from the Szeto-Schiller family of mitochondria-targeted peptides. It is cell-permeable and concentrates at the inner mitochondrial membrane, where it binds cardiolipin, a lipid found almost only in that membrane. Research uses it to study cardiolipin, membrane structure and mitochondrial function in cell and animal models

MOTS-c

A sixteen-amino-acid peptide encoded within mitochondrial DNA, in the gene for 12S ribosomal RNA. It was first described in 2015 by researchers at the University of Southern California, and belongs to a small group of mitochondrial-derived peptides. Most published work examines metabolic signaling, including the AMPK pathway, in mouse and cell models.

SLU-PP-332

Not a peptide either. SLU-PP-332 is a small synthetic molecule developed at Saint Louis University that activates estrogen-related receptors, which despite the name do not respond to estrogen and help regulate genes involved in mitochondrial and oxidative metabolism. It is a preclinical tool compound: published work is in cultured cells and mice, and there is no published human data.

NAD+

Not a peptide. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide is a coenzyme that carries electrons in the reactions mitochondria use to produce ATP, and is also used by enzymes such as sirtuins. Research on NAD+ looks at how its levels change across tissues and conditions in cell and animal models, and how those changes relate to metabolic measures

About the Peptides in This Category

BPC-157

BPC-157 is a synthetic peptide of 15 amino acids. Its sequence comes from a larger protein found in human gastric juice, and the name stands for body protection compound. Thymosin Beta-4 and TB-500

Thymosin beta-4 is a 43-amino-acid protein found in nearly every cell. It was first characterized from calf thymus, hence the name, but its main role is binding actin, the protein that forms the cell's internal scaffolding. TB-500 is a different molecule: a synthetic seven-amino-acid copy of the actin-binding region. Thymosin beta-4 has been through early clinical trials as a pharmaceutical eye drop. What are Tissue Repair Compounds?

Tissue Repair Compounds is our category for peptides used in laboratory research on how cells and tissues respond to injury. It holds BPC-157, a 15-amino-acid peptide; thymosin beta-4, a 43-amino-acid protein; TB-500, a seven-amino-acid fragment of thymosin beta-4; and two blends that combine these with GHK-Cu and KPV. Most published findings come from cell cultures and rodent models, and human data are limited or absent. Supplied for laboratory research use only, not for human or veterinary use.

How Do Tissue Repair Compounds Work?

Each peptide is studied through a different mechanism, and none is fully understood. Thymosin beta-4 binds actin, the protein that forms the cell's internal scaffolding, which is why research links it to how cells change shape and move. TB-500 copies the part of thymosin beta-4 that binds actin. For BPC-157, rodent studies point to blood vessel formation and growth factor signaling, but the mechanism is still debated. KPV is studied for inflammatory signaling in gut cells, and GHK-Cu for how it binds copper. These descriptions come from cell and animal research and establish no use outside the laboratory.

All four products ship as lyophilized powder in sealed vials. Before reconstitution, store them refrigerated, away from light, heat and moisture. Add the water slowly down the inside wall of the vial and swirl gently rather than shaking. Once reconstituted, keep the vial refrigerated and use it within the window your protocol sets. The KLOW blend contains GHK-Cu, which gives the solution a blue color. That color comes from the copper and is expected.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are Copper & Dermatological Peptides?

Copper & Dermatological Peptides is our category for peptides used in laboratory research on skin cells, connective tissue and pigmentation. It holds GHK-Cu, a copper-binding tripeptide; GLOW, a blend of GHK-Cu with BPC-157 and TB-500; and melanotan II, a synthetic analogue of a hormone involved in pigmentation. All are made by peptide synthesis and supplied as lyophilized powder. None is a cosmetic or skin care product, and most published findings come from cell cultures and animal models. Supplied for laboratory research use only, not for human or veterinary use.

How Do Copper & Dermatological Peptides Work?

Each compound is studied through a different mechanism. GHK-Cu binds copper tightly and holds it in a form that does not drive the harmful reactions loose copper can. In fibroblast studies it is linked to changes in collagen and matrix production and in the activity of many genes. BPC-157 and TB-500, the other two GLOW components, are studied mainly in rodent injury models. Melanotan II activates melanocortin receptors, including MC1R on pigment cells, which controls melanin production. These descriptions come from cell and animal research and establish no use outside the laboratory.

How are Copper & Dermatological Peptides Typically Stored and Handled?

All products in this category ship as lyophilized powder in sealed vials. Store them refrigerated from arrival, away from light, heat and moisture, and keep each vial sealed until reconstitution; freezing the dry powder is an option for longer storage. Bacteriostatic water is the usual fluid, and our vials hold 3 ml, so reconstitution volumes stay within that. Add the water slowly down the inside wall of the vial and swirl gently rather than shaking. GHK-Cu and GLOW give a blue solution because of the copper, which is expected.

What are the Common Research Applications of Copper & Dermatological Peptides?

Published laboratory work in this area falls into a few groups. Fibroblast studies measure collagen, glycosaminoglycan and decorin production. Wound studies, mostly in rats and rabbits, track closure and new blood vessel growth. Antioxidant studies look at enzyme levels and inflammatory markers in cultured cells. Gene-expression studies have mapped which genes shift in the presence of GHK. Hair follicle studies in rodents form a smaller, separate line of work. Pigmentation research on melanotan II measures melanocortin receptor activity and melanin production in pigment cells. Results from cell and animal models describe skin biology, not effects in a person.

When Can I Expect My Copper & Dermatological Peptides Delivery?

Orders are typically delivered within 2–4 business days from the date the order is placed. Delivery is within Costa Rica only. Timing can vary with carrier schedules, the delivery province and order processing. We confirm stock and the expected delivery window with you before an order is finalized.

Growth Hormone Secretagogues

Growth hormone secretagogues are compounds that prompt the pituitary gland to release growth hormone. This category holds both main kinds used in laboratory research, GHRH analogues such as sermorelin, tesamorelin and CJC-1295, and the ghrelin-receptor peptide ipamorelin, plus IGF-1 LR3, a related compound that acts further down the same pathway. Peptides Costa Rica supplies them as research-grade material, with independent batch testing and delivery within Costa Rica. Everything here is supplied for laboratory research use only.

What Growth Hormone Secretagogues Are

The pituitary gland releases growth hormone in pulses, under two main signals. GHRH, growth hormone-releasing hormone from the brain, switches release on through its own receptor. Ghrelin, made mainly in the stomach, adds a second signal through the ghrelin receptor. Secretagogues are synthetic peptides built to act on one of those two receptors.

That makes them different from somatropin, which is the growth hormone itself. A secretagogue works upstream, at the pituitary, so research on them focuses on how the release signal is controlled.

At Peptides Costa Rica, we supply these compounds for research purposes. We focus on clear pricing, honest product details, and reliable local service for customers in Costa Rica.

Buy Growth Hormone Secretagogues: Research Grade & Lab Tested

This category holds seven products across three compound types. Sermorelin, tesamorelin (in two vial sizes) and CJC-1295 with DAC are analogues of GHRH, the hormone that signals the pituitary to release growth hormone. Ipamorelin is a five-amino-acid peptide that acts on the ghrelin receptor instead. One vial combines CJC-1295 without DAC with ipamorelin. IGF-1 LR3 is not a secretagogue at all: it is an engineered form of IGF-1, which sits further down the same pathway. Every product ships as a lyophilized powder in a sealed vial, and most are reconstituted with bacteriostatic water before laboratory use.

Every batch is tested by an independent laboratory for identity and purity, and the certificate of analysis is available for the lot you receive. Prices are listed per vial on each product page. Delivery is within Costa Rica only and usually takes two to four business days, with free shipping on orders above $200 and bulk pricing on five or more vials of the same product. Our team can confirm availability, vial size and the expected delivery window before you order.

About the Compounds in This Category

GHRH Analogues

Sermorelin is the first 29 amino acids of natural GHRH. Tesamorelin is the full 44-amino-acid GHRH with a stabilizing chemical group added to the front end. CJC-1295 has four amino acid swaps, and the with-DAC form binds albumin in the blood, so it circulates for days.

Ipamorelin

Ipamorelin is a five-amino-acid peptide first developed by Novo Nordisk in the late 1990s. It acts on the ghrelin receptor, a separate route into the pituitary. In animal studies, unlike older releasing peptides, it did not raise cortisol.

IGF-1 LR3

IGF-1 is made mainly in the liver in response to growth hormone. IGF-1 LR3 is an engineered 83-amino-acid version that largely escapes the binding proteins that normally hold IGF-1 in check. Its best-established use is in cell culture media.

Reading the Research

Much of the human research on this class comes from clinical settings and does not transfer to research material. Findings in cells and animals describe how a hormone system works. They are not evidence of any effect in a person.

What are Growth Hormone Secretagogue?

Growth hormone secretagogues are synthetic peptides that act on the pituitary gland to trigger the release of growth hormone. There are two main kinds. GHRH analogues, such as sermorelin, tesamorelin and CJC-1295, copy the brain's own release signal. Ghrelin-receptor agonists, such as ipamorelin, act through a second receptor. This category also holds IGF-1 LR3, which is not a secretagogue but an engineered form of IGF-1, the hormone that growth hormone signals the liver to make. Supplied for laboratory research use only, not for human or veterinary use.

How Do Growth Hormone Secretagogue Work?

In research models, GHRH analogues bind the GHRH receptor on the growth hormone-producing cells of the pituitary, which triggers release of stored hormone. Ipamorelin binds the ghrelin receptor, a separate route that works alongside the GHRH signal. Growth hormone then acts on its own receptor around the body, and one of the main downstream results is IGF-1, produced largely in the liver. IGF-1 LR3 enters the pathway at that later stage and binds the IGF-1 receptor directly. None of them acts directly on muscle. These descriptions come from cell and animal research and establish no use outside the laboratory.

How are Growth Hormone Secretagogue Typically Stored and Handled?

Published laboratory work on this class falls into a few areas. Receptor studies measure how each compound binds the GHRH receptor or the ghrelin receptor. Pituitary studies track growth hormone release from cells in culture. Animal studies follow the timing and size of growth hormone pulses and the IGF-1 response downstream. Pharmacology studies compare how long each compound lasts in circulation, which is where CJC-1295 with DAC differs most from the rest. IGF-1 LR3 is also widely used as a supplement in cell culture media. Results from cell and animal models describe a hormone system, not effects in a person.

Copper peptides are studied for the part they play in collagen production, tissue repair and cell renewal. They form when a short peptide chain binds a copper ion, and that pairing is what makes them useful to researchers working with skin and connective tissue models.

Peptides Costa Rica supplies copper peptides as research-grade material. They are produced by solid-phase peptide synthesis, not extracted from human or animal tissue, and arrive as a lyophilized powder in a sealed vial. The powder is reconstituted with bacteriostatic water before use, which lets a laboratory prepare the concentration a protocol calls for. Every batch is tested by an independent laboratory for identity and purity, and the certificate of analysis is available through our COA database, so the material entering a study is documented from the start.

What Copper Peptides Are Studied For

Copper peptide research, and GHK-Cu research in particular, has concentrated on skin, connective tissue and repair models. These are the areas that come up most often in the published literature:

 

Collagen and Skin Models

In cultured skin fibroblasts, GHK-Cu has been reported to increase the synthesis of collagen, glycosaminoglycans and decorin, the proteins and sugars that give skin its structure and elasticity. These changes show up at very low concentrations, which is part of why the tripeptide has held research attention for five decades.

Tissue Repair

Animal wound models are the most studied application. In rat and rabbit studies, wounds treated with GHK-Cu showed faster contraction, quicker granulation tissue formation and better blood vessel development than untreated controls. Researchers connect this to shifts in the genes that control how the matrix is broken down and rebuilt.

Antioxidant Activity

Copper held by the GHK tripeptide is redox-silenced, meaning it does not drive the free-radical reactions that loose copper ions can. In study models the complex raised levels of antioxidant enzymes and lowered inflammatory markers such as TNF-alpha, which is why it appears regularly in oxidative stress research.

Hair Follicle Models

Follicle work is an active but much smaller field. In rodent studies, copper peptides applied to the skin were reported to enlarge follicle size and move follicles into their growth phase. Controlled human data is limited, so this remains an open research question rather than a settled finding.

What are Copper Peptides?

Copper peptides are short amino acid chains that hold a copper ion. The best known is GHK-Cu: glycine, histidine and lysine bound to copper. How Do Copper Peptides Work?

In study models, the peptide acts as a carrier: it holds copper in a stable, redox-silenced form and presents it to cells. Copper is a cofactor for enzymes involved in building and cross-linking connective tissue, including lysyl oxidase and superoxide dismutase. Copper peptides ship as a lyophilized powder, and in that dry, sealed state they stay stable for a long time when kept cool, dry and out of direct light. Most laboratories refrigerate unopened vials, or freeze them for longer storage, and keep the vial sealed until the moment of reconstitution so moisture and contaminants stay out. Bacteriostatic water is the standard reconstitution fluid, and our vials hold 3 ml, so reconstitution volumes stay within that. Once in solution the vial is refrigerated and used within the window set by the protocol, since peptides degrade faster wet than dry. GHK-Cu solutions carry a distinctive blue colour from the bound copper, and a sharp change in colour or clarity is a reason to discard the vial.

What are the Common Research Applications of Copper Peptides?

Published work falls into a few clear areas. Skin and fibroblast studies measure collagen, elastin and glycosaminoglycan production and how the surrounding matrix is remodeled. Wound-healing models in rats and rabbits track contraction rate, granulation tissue and blood vessel formation. Gene-expression work profiles which genes shift in response to the peptide, particularly those tied to repair, inflammation and antioxidant defense. Cosmetic science groups study copper peptides as raw ingredients, including stability and formulation behavior. A smaller body of follicle research looks at growth-phase activity in rodent models. All of this is laboratory research, and none of it establishes human use.

When Can I Expect My Copper Peptides Delivery?

Orders are typically delivered within 2–4 business days from the date the order is placed. Delivery is within Costa Rica only. Timing can vary with carrier schedules, the delivery province and order processing. We confirm stock and the expected delivery window before an order is finalized.
